verdict.rationale: Proa's template macro validates templates at compile time and consolidates static markup. Adding signals and event handlers makes Proa emit per-island vanilla-JS modules on a roughly 1.3 KB shared runtime, which points to compiler-generated, signal-driven DOM updates rather than a VDOM library. However, the compile-time optimization evidence covers server HTML output, and no source says how client DOM updates happen or that there is no diffing step. Missing for 10: explicit documentation that island DOM updates avoid virtual-DOM diffing, a description of the client update mechanism, and independent or benchmark corroboration of client-side update performance.
